scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requests an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing wrong bills (CL-01) — this is the requester's framing, not an established mechanism, and conflates diagnosis with automated bill remediation that K-BILLWRITE forbids.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled starting August and kept rising into September: 610, 590, 1180, 1260 disputes/month (E-05)
A majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) are tied to ACTUAL meter reads versus 1240 to ESTIMATED reads (E-02)
Field manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-03)
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled since August (E-05: 610→590→1180→1260/month) because the majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025, E-02) are tied to ACTUAL meter reads, not estimate substitutions — ruling out tariff changes (E-01) and making AMI/field read-capture gaps insufficient as the dominant cause. Current evidence best supports that a change to billing import validation rules around August (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE) is causing otherwise-valid ACTUAL reads to be rejected or mishandled during billing import, producing incorrect bills that customers then dispute; a secondary minority of disputes (1240 ESTIMATED-read bills) is driven by a field-staffing route-completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95 target, E-03).

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-02 revised by E-11: The counts still stand: 1240 disputed bills are ESTIMATED-read and 1785 are ACTUAL-read. It no longer means the ESTIMATED/ACTUAL split marks a mechanism boundary between read-capture-gap and billing-rule causes, because E-11 shows 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED bills are themselves billing-import rejections of valid AMI reads (same REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION mechanism as the ACTUAL majority); only 56 are true missing-read cases.

problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled since August 2026 (610→590→1180→1260/month, E-05) because the billing-import high-consumption validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-12), compares raw unscaled meter register values against 12-month m3 consumption history; since firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out June 2026) report readings in a register unit of 0.1 m3 rather than the m3 unit legacy firmware uses (E-13), BV-17 misclassifies legitimate v4.2 readings as high-consumption outliers and rejects them (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) at billing import. This rejection mechanism directly produced estimate substitution for 1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-11, superseding the field-staffing explanation), and the same billing-import mechanism is also implicated in the bulk of the 1785 disputed ACTUAL-read bills (E-02 revised), so roughly 98% of disputed bills trace to this one BV-17/firmware unit-mismatch, driving customers to dispute the resulting incorrect bills.

H-WRONG-BILLS-AUTOFIX.statement: Dispute volume doubled since August because bills themselves are incorrect, and an automated agent can identify and fix the cause plus auto-answer tickets.

H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: An AMI/MDMS read delivery or validation failure starting around August is causing estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter reads (contracted to ORG-FIELD) are not being uploaded or are invalid since August, causing estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August is causing valid reads to be rejected or mishandled, producing wrong bills.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: Reduced field staffing/route completion is lowering manual read capture rates, increasing estimated (and disputed) bills.

H-CS-PROCESS-BACKLOG.statement: Bills may be largely correct; the apparent 'dispute surge' reflects slower or less effective ticket handling/response process rather than a billing-accuracy problem.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT.statement: Billing import rejects AMI reads flagged as high-consumption outliers (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), causing accepted-but-rejected reads to be billed as ESTIMATED and subsequently disputed.

H-BV17-UNIT-MISMATCH.statement: BV-17's comparison of raw (unscaled) register value against 12-month m3 history, deployed 2026-08-01, misclassifies legitimate high readings as high-consumption outliers, producing the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections seen in E-11 and driving the August dispute surge (E-05).

H-ACTUAL-DISTINCT-CAUSE.statement: The 1785 disputed ACTUAL-read bills are not produced via the BV-17/firmware-v4.2 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pathway, which structurally always yields ESTIMATED billing per E-14, and likely stem from a distinct, as-yet-unconfirmed cause.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Billing-db's tariff_change_log has zero records, so no tariff/rate changes occurred that could explain wrong bills or the dispute surge. This rules out tariff changes as a cause, narrowing the search to read capture (AMI/field), billing import validation, or ticket-handling process explanations already under consideration.

Among disputed bills, 1785 are tied to ACTUAL reads versus 1240 tied to ESTIMATED reads, so a majority of disputes involve bills built from accepted/actual meter reads rather than estimate substitutions. This means read-capture gaps (AMI delivery or field read failures, which only matter when a read is missing and an estimate is substituted) can account for at most the 1240 estimated-read disputes, not the larger ACTUAL-read share.

The counts still stand: 1240 disputed bills are ESTIMATED-read and 1785 are ACTUAL-read. It no longer means the ESTIMATED/ACTUAL split marks a mechanism boundary between read-capture-gap and billing-rule causes, because E-11 shows 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED bills are themselves billing-import rejections of valid AMI reads (same REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION mechanism as the ACTUAL majority); only 56 are true missing-read cases.

Field route completion was 88% against a 95% target in Aug-Sep 2026 across 9200 manual-read accounts, showing a genuine manual-read capture shortfall during the dispute-surge window. This supports a field-read-failure/staffing mechanism as a partial cause, but per E-02 it can only account for the minority (ESTIMATED-read) share of disputes, not the ACTUAL-read majority.

The observation still stands: route completion was 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts in Aug-Sep 2026, a genuine route-completion shortfall. It no longer means this shortfall is the mechanism behind the 1240-bill ESTIMATED-read dispute bucket, because E-11 shows only 56 of those 1240 (NO_READ_RECEIVED) fit a true missing-read mechanism, so the field-staffing driver can explain at most a small fraction, not the secondary mechanism claimed in PR-ROOT/PR-CHAIN-4.

CRM dispute_response_times (E-04) shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, i.e. response handling is operating within SLA despite the volume surge. This weakens the framing that a slow or ineffective ticket-response process (rather than billing accuracy) explains the dispute surge.

crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly shows 610 (Jun), 590 (Jul), 1180 (Aug), 1260 (Sep) disputes, i.e. monthly volume roughly doubled starting August and continued rising into September. This numerically substantiates the magnitude of the 'doubled since August' claim but says nothing about its cause.

For the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-02), AMI read-event data shows 1184 had an AMI read received before cutoff but rejected at billing import under status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while only 56 had no AMI read received at all (NO_READ_RECEIVED). E-12.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-config's validation_rule_changes log shows rule BV-17 (high-consumption check comparing raw register value against 12-month m3 history, with no unit scaling) was deployed 2026-08-01, timing-aligned with the dispute-surge onset (E-05); the only other record, BV-09, is a cosmetic label change deployed in March and is not causally relevant. This authoritative, complete record identifies a concrete, named rule change coinciding with August and plausibly explains the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections already observed in E-11, confirming the DA-RULES-log check that A-RULE-CHANGE-TIMING flagged as outstanding; it does not by itself confirm account-scope correlation with the disputed bills.

The observation still stands: billing-config's validation_rule_changes shows BV-17 (raw-value vs 12-month m3 history, no unit scaling) deployed 2026-08-01, timing-aligned with the surge onset (E-05); BV-09 remains a cosmetic, causally irrelevant change. It no longer supports extending BV-17's confirmed rejection mechanism to the 1785 disputed ACTUAL-read bills, because E-14 shows billing-db's affected_accounts_v42 (the actual footprint of this rejection pathway) is 100% ESTIMATED-read with zero ACTUAL-read accounts.

This gives a verified mechanism for how BV-17's unscaled raw-value-vs-m3-history comparison (E-12) could misclassify legitimate v4.2 meter readings as high-consumption outliers, matching the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections already observed (E-11).

U-RULECHANGE.question: What specifically changed in billing import validation rules around August, and does its timing/account scope align with the ACTUAL-read disputed bills?
U-RULECHANGE.decision_impact: Confirms or refutes the primary root-cause mechanism (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE); if the rule change does not align with ACTUAL-read disputes, diagnostic scope must pivot before any remediation is scoped.
U-RULECHANGE.resolution_path: Query billing-config rule_change_log entries around August and correlate change timestamps/account scope against disputed ACTUAL-read bill accounts in DA-BILL.
U-RULECHANGE.safe_placeholder: Treat the rule-change mechanism as a working hypothesis only: proceed with diagnostic investigation of DA-RULES, draft no remediation and request no bill writes until the mechanism is confirmed.
U-RULECHANGE.resolution: billing-config confirms BV-17 (high-consumption check, raw register value vs 12-month m3 history, unit_scaling=none) was deployed 2026-08-01, answering 'what changed' and confirming timing alignment with the August surge (E-05); account-scope alignment with the ACTUAL-read disputed bills is not yet confirmed by this record alone.

U-FIELDOVERLAP.question: Is the field-staffing route-completion shortfall (E-03) an independent contributor to the ESTIMATED-read minority, or does it overlap with/compound the billing-rule-change effect?
U-FIELDOVERLAP.decision_impact: Determines whether field-staffing shortfall needs its own route-completion remediation or just compounds the billing-rule effect, affecting whether push_route_update is actually warranted.
U-FIELDOVERLAP.resolution_path: Cross-reference route-log completion-shortfall accounts against billing-config rule-change-affected accounts to determine overlap.
U-FIELDOVERLAP.safe_placeholder: Treat the two mechanisms as independently contributing until overlap is measured; do not scale back the field-staffing investigation on the strength of the rule-change hypothesis alone.
U-FIELDOVERLAP.resolution: AMI read-event data for disputed ESTIMATED bills (E-11) shows only 56 of 1240 have no read received at all; the remaining 1184 had a read rejected at billing import, so the field-staffing/route-completion shortfall is at most an independent driver for a small residual (56), not the dominant mechanism for the ESTIMATED-read bucket.

U-METRICCOVERAGE.question: Does dispute ticket volume capture all wrong bills, or do some billing-rule-caused errors go uncontested and thus understate the true wrong-bill rate?
U-METRICCOVERAGE.decision_impact: Affects whether M-TICKETVOL/M-ACTUALRATE validly measure the scope of the billing-accuracy problem or only the contested subset.
U-METRICCOVERAGE.resolution_path: Compare the full billing-db REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION/affected_accounts population against DA-TICKET to estimate the uncontested error rate.
U-METRICCOVERAGE.safe_placeholder: Treat ticket-based metrics as a lower bound on billing errors, not a complete count.

U-AMIACCESS.question: Could a residual AMI-side issue still be relevant to the ACTUAL-read bucket given mdms-export access provisioning (E-10) is only a non-authoritative stakeholder claim?
U-AMIACCESS.decision_impact: If access is not actually provisioned, mdms-export queries for the ACTUAL-read investigation may fail or return incomplete data.
U-AMIACCESS.resolution_path: Confirm MDMS export access via an authoritative mdms-export tool call rather than relying on SH-AMI's claim (E-10).
U-AMIACCESS.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-db/billing-config analysis first; treat MDMS-dependent queries as blocked until access is tool-confirmed.

U-ACTUALCORRELATION.question: Does the BV-17/firmware v4.2 unit-mismatch mechanism, confirmed via account-level AMI read-event data for the ESTIMATED-read bucket (E-11), also hold at the account level for the 1785 disputed ACTUAL-read bills, or do some of those have a distinct cause?
U-ACTUALCORRELATION.decision_impact: Determines whether BV-17/firmware remediation covers nearly all disputes or only the ESTIMATED-read minority, affecting prioritization of any rule-correction escalation and the true scope of the billing error.
U-ACTUALCORRELATION.resolution_path: Query billing-db and mdms-export for account-level firmware version and billing_import_status on the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills and compare timing/overlap with BV-17 deployment (E-12).
U-ACTUALCORRELATION.safe_placeholder: Treat BV-17/firmware mismatch as the primary working hypothesis for all disputed bills while continuing ticket-response mitigation; do not scope any bill correction until confirmed.
U-ACTUALCORRELATION.resolution: billing-db's complete affected_accounts_v42 view shows zero ACTUAL-read accounts among the 1184 BV-17/firmware-v4.2 rejected accounts, suggesting the confirmed mechanism does not extend to the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills, which likely have a distinct, still-unconfirmed cause; a direct mdms-export join against the 1785 ACTUAL accounts is still needed for full confirmation.

U-ACTUALCAUSE.question: What specific mechanism produces the 1785 disputed ACTUAL-read bills, given E-14 confirms they are not produced via the BV-17/firmware v4.2 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pathway?
U-ACTUALCAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether any remedy can address the majority of disputes; without it only the ~1184 ESTIMATED-read REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION bills can be remediated, leaving the larger ACTUAL-read share unaddressed.
U-ACTUALCAUSE.resolution_path: Query billing-db/billing-config for other validation codes, tariff flags, or consumption anomalies specific to the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed accounts and compare against billing-rule change timing.
U-ACTUALCAUSE.safe_placeholder: Limit any remediation claims and ticket-response templates to the confirmed BV-17/firmware v4.2 ESTIMATED-read scope; do not represent the ACTUAL-read majority as explained or fixed.

A-RULE-CHANGE-TIMING.statement: The billing import validation rule change (if any) occurred around August, coinciding with the dispute surge onset; timing alignment is inferred from the surge (E-05), not yet confirmed against the DA-RULES log.

A-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-MECHAN.statement: The field route completion shortfall is the mechanism behind the ESTIMATED-read minority of disputes, consistent with SH-FIELD's non-authoritative claim.

A-DISPUTE-TICKET-PROXY.statement: CRM dispute ticket volume is a reasonable proxy for the underlying billing-accuracy problem rather than purely a reporting/behavioral artifact.

A-ACTUAL-BUCKET-MECHANISM.statement: The BV-17/firmware v4.2 unit-mismatch rejection mechanism confirmed account-by-account for the ESTIMATED-read bucket (E-11) also accounts for the majority of the 1785 disputed ACTUAL-read bills, rather than those having a separate, unconfirmed cause.

symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled starting August and continued rising into September: 610, 590, 1180, 1260 disputes/month (E-05).
1240 of 3025 disputed bills are ESTIMATED-read and 1785 are ACTUAL-read (E-02); the ACTUAL-read bucket is the larger share.

1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes are confirmed, account-by-account, to be REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections of valid AMI reads from firmware-v4.2 meters, not true missing-read cases (E-11, E-14).

The confirmed BV-17/firmware-v4.2 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pathway (affected_accounts_v42) is 100% ESTIMATED-read, with zero ACTUAL-read accounts, so it cannot by itself account for the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (E-14).

problem_definition.root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled since August 2026 (610→590→1180→1260/month, E-05), spanning 1240 ESTIMATED-read and 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (E-02). Account-level evidence confirms billing-import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-12), which compares raw unscaled register values to 12-month m3 history, misclassifies firmware-v4.2 meters' 0.1 m3-unit readings (E-13) as high-consumption outliers and rejects them under REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION at import (E-11); this pathway produced exactly 1184 affected accounts, all billed ESTIMATED (E-14), accounting for the bulk of the ESTIMATED-read disputes. This confirmed mechanism structurally always yields ESTIMATED billing and therefore cannot explain the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills — the larger share of the surge — whose cause is distinct from BV-17/firmware-v4.2 and not yet established by evidence (E-14).

proposal.root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled since August 2026 (610→590→1180→1260/month, E-05), spanning 1240 ESTIMATED-read and 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (E-02). Account-level evidence confirms billing-import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-12), which compares raw unscaled register values to 12-month m3 history, misclassifies firmware-v4.2 meters' 0.1 m3-unit readings (E-13) as high-consumption outliers and rejects them under REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION at import (E-11); this pathway produced exactly 1184 affected accounts, all billed ESTIMATED (E-14), accounting for the bulk of the ESTIMATED-read disputes. This confirmed mechanism structurally always yields ESTIMATED billing and therefore cannot explain the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills — the larger share of the surge — whose cause is distinct from BV-17/firmware-v4.2 and not yet established by evidence (E-14).
proposal.requested_solution: SH-CS requests an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing wrong bills (CL-01); this conflates ticket response with automated bill remediation, which K-BILLWRITE forbids without SH-BILL authorization, and already assumed a single root cause that E-14 has since disproven for most of the surge.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled starting August and continued rising into September: 610, 590, 1180, 1260 disputes/month (E-05).
1240 of 3025 disputed bills are ESTIMATED-read and 1785 are ACTUAL-read (E-02); the ACTUAL-read bucket is the larger share.

1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes are confirmed, account-by-account, to be REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections of valid AMI reads from firmware-v4.2 meters, not true missing-read cases (E-11, E-14).

The confirmed BV-17/firmware-v4.2 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pathway (affected_accounts_v42) is 100% ESTIMATED-read, with zero ACTUAL-read accounts, so it cannot by itself account for the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (E-14).
Dispute response times remain within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d, E-04), so the surge is not explained by slower ticket handling.
causal_chain: Firmware v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) report register readings in units of 0.1 m3 instead of the m3 unit legacy firmware uses (E-13).
Billing import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares the raw unscaled register value against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-12).
This mismatch causes BV-17 to misclassify legitimate v4.2 high readings as high-consumption outliers and reject them at import under REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-11).
Account-level data confirms this pathway produced exactly 1184 affected accounts, 100% of which are billed ESTIMATED (E-14) — the mechanism structurally always yields ESTIMATED billing.
These 1184 accounts correspond to the bulk (1184 of 1240) of the disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, which customers then dispute via CRM (E-11, E-02).

The 1785 disputed ACTUAL-read bills — the larger share of the 3025 total disputed bills — do not appear in this REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION/firmware-v4.2 account set (E-14) and are not produced by this confirmed mechanism.
Their cause remains distinct and unconfirmed (H-ACTUAL-DISTINCT-CAUSE), while total dispute ticket volume continues at roughly double the pre-August baseline (E-05).

key_points: Original request (claim CL-01, from SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and auto-fix whatever causes wrong bills; dispute ticket volume roughly doubled since August (evidence E-05: 610, 590, 1180, 1260 tickets/month).

Investigation confirmed billing-import rule BV-17 (E-12, deployed 2026-08-01) combined with a firmware v4.2 meter unit mismatch (E-13) causes REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections, producing 1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-11).

An earlier hypothesis that this same BV-17/firmware mechanism also explained the larger 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed-bill bucket was invalidated: evidence E-14 shows the mechanism's actual account footprint is 100% ESTIMATED-read with zero ACTUAL-read accounts.
The cause of the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills remains unresolved: verification obligation VOB-U-ACTUALCAUSE is CRITICAL and was required before release, but its status is OPEN.

What was released (per SolutionDesign SD-3) is limited to two actions: cross-referencing AMI reads against disputed ACTUAL-read accounts (DA-MDMS) and drafting dispute-ticket response templates (DA-TICKET); no automated bill writes or dispatch changes are included.

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds; the open VOB-U-ACTUALCAUSE's blocking scope (analyze_disputed_actual_read_bills, review_billing_import_validation_codes) falls outside the actions actually released.

The original auto-fix request from SH-CS was not fulfilled as asked: constraint K-BILLWRITE forbids automated bill writes without Billing Operations (SH-BILL) authorization, and the single-root-cause premise behind the request was disproven by E-14.
The DEFINE gate for this problem definition reached only CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully resolved before release.
limitations_explained: Structural fixes — patching BV-17 for firmware-aware unit conversion, an interim bypass for firmware v4.2 meters, and mass rebilling of affected accounts — were all assessed as infeasible within the available contest time/tooling, so none were built or deployed.

The released diagnostic correlation work can only narrow or help identify the cause of the ACTUAL-read dispute bucket; it cannot itself fix that cause, and the underlying question (VOB-U-ACTUALCAUSE) remains OPEN.

Bills already issued incorrectly to the 1184 confirmed firmware-v4.2/ESTIMATED accounts still require manual correction by Billing Operations under constraint K-BILLWRITE; no bill was or could be auto-corrected by this release.
The dispute-ticket response templates produced are a stopgap to hold response-time SLA, not a resolution of the underlying billing-accuracy problem causing the disputes.
Ticket-volume-based metrics may have coverage gaps and should not be treated as a complete measure of billing accuracy, since some billing errors could go uncontested.

Dispute ticket volume is only expected to return toward the pre-August baseline after both the confirmed BV-17/firmware cause and the still-unidentified ACTUAL-read cause are remediated; remediation of only one cause may not restore the baseline.
The DEFINE phase gate itself returned only a CONDITIONAL_PASS rather than a full pass, with several items deferred into tracked verification obligations instead of being closed before this release.
proposal.summary: SH-CS (claim CL-01) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and auto-fix the cause of wrong bills, after dispute volume roughly doubled since August (E-05). Investigation found billing-import rule BV-17 (E-12) plus a firmware v4.2 unit mismatch (E-13) causes REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections confirmed, account-by-account, for 1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-11). An earlier version of the problem definition extended this mechanism to also explain the larger 1785-bill ACTUAL-read bucket, but evidence E-14 showed the mechanism's confirmed footprint is 100% ESTIMATED-read with zero ACTUAL-read accounts, invalidating that claim and leaving the ACTUAL-read cause an open critical unknown (VOB-U-ACTUALCAUSE). Because the request conflated ticket-answering with automated bill fixes (forbidden without authorization by constraint K-BILLWRITE) and rested on a disproven single-cause premise, the full auto-fix was not built. What was released (design SD-3) is narrower: a diagnostic cross-reference of AMI reads against ACTUAL-read disputed accounts (DA-MDMS) and dispute-ticket response templates (DA-TICKET). The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, no holds, because the still-open VOB-U-ACTUALCAUSE's blocking scope falls outside what is actually released. Documented limitations include: structural remedies (BV-17 patch, interim bypass, mass rebilling) are infeasible in contest time; the diagnostic work can narrow but not fix the ACTUAL-read cause; already-issued wrong bills for the 1184 confirmed accounts still need manual Billing Operations correction; templates are only an SLA stopgap; ticket metrics may miss uncontested errors; and ticket volume is only expected to normalize once both causes are remediated.
